title: Research Note: The Physics of Coexistence — Force, Charge, Mass, and Time in Satta–Unit Interaction

passages.section: Introduction
passages.text: Scope: Every explicit statement located in the primary texts (SB, MVD, JV, AVD, JVD, KD) that uses physics vocabulary — pressure, motion, force, magnetism, electricity, heat, charge/excitation (āvesh — context-dependent, see §8), mass, weight, gravitation, atomic structure (nucleus, orbits, elements, and the nature of the constituent particle/ansh itself), states of matter, density, radioactivity, indestructibility/conservation, cosmogony, time — to describe either (a) how satta (Omnipotence/Omnipresence) and units (ikai) relate, or (b) how units relate to one another. Citations use the project’s tag system (SB = Samadhanatmak Bhautikvad / “Resolution Centred Materialism”; MVD = Madhyasth Darshan Coexistentialism; JV = Jeevan Vidya: An Introduction; AVD = Adhyatmvad; JVD = Janvad; KD = Manav Karm Darshan, Hindi-only — KD quotes are our working translations; full working translation in References/Madhyasth-Darshan/KD-Karm-Darshan-English/KD-Karm-Darshan-English.md, see Method note) with page numbers verified directly against the source PDFs (see Method note at the end).

passages.section: Introduction
passages.text: Structure. Every numbered section and subsection below is split into two clearly separated parts: What MD says — a numbered list of paraphrased claims taken from the primary texts, each with a page citation — and Our reading — this note’s own interpretation, cross-references, and flagged tensions. Treat the numbered claims as the raw material to re-verify against the source PDFs before quoting in a catalog Study (via Scripts/_quote_tool.py verify); treat “Our reading” as commentary, not text. §14 (Synthesis) and §15 (Open Tensions) are, by their nature, entirely “Our reading” — there is no separate claims list for them.

passages.section: Introduction
passages.text: KD’s stated core principle (siddhant, title page) is śram–gati–pariṇām — effort–motion–result — the same triple SB p. 62 unfolds from saturation (§4). Its section 3 (chapters 3.1–3.15) is the most physics-dense stretch anywhere in the corpus: atomic structure (ch. 3.1, p. 53), development in the atom (3.2, p. 59), heat and the Earth’s balance (3.7, p. 72), state–motion (3.8, p. 83), quantity (3.9, p. 87), force–power (3.11, p. 101), reflection–projection (3.12, p. 109), pressure/flow/wave/electromagnetic force (3.13, p. 117), place–direction–distance–area–angle (3.14, p. 124), and time (3.15, p. 133).

passages.heading: 1-the-base-claim-two-poles-one-coexistence
passages.section: 1. The base claim: two poles, one coexistence
passages.text: Everything below sits on top of one recurring assertion: existence has exactly two aspects — formless, actionless satta and formful, active prakriti (nature, as countless units) — and neither produces the other.

passages.heading: 1-the-base-claim-two-poles-one-coexistence
passages.section: 1. The base claim: two poles, one coexistence
passages.text: What MD says:

passages.heading: 1-the-base-claim-two-poles-one-coexistence
passages.section: 1. The base claim: two poles, one coexistence
passages.text: Consciousness (Omnipotence, satta) and matter are inseparably present; all of existence is, in essence, nature (matter) saturated in Omnipotence (consciousness) — neither is ever observed arising from the other (SB, p. 48).

passages.heading: 1-the-base-claim-two-poles-one-coexistence
passages.section: 1. The base claim: two poles, one coexistence
passages.text: Omnipotence itself is formless and omnipresent; nature within it is endowed with form, properties, essential nature, and dharma, and is inseparable from it — there is no place where Omnipotence is absent (SB, p. 48).

passages.heading: 1-the-base-claim-two-poles-one-coexistence
passages.section: 1. The base claim: two poles, one coexistence
passages.text: Nature, saturated in Omnipotence, exists as countless discrete units, each one surrounded, submerged, and soaked in it (SB, p. 48).

passages.heading: 1-the-base-claim-two-poles-one-coexistence
passages.section: 1. The base claim: two poles, one coexistence
passages.text: Our reading: The relation-word the texts use for this bond is samprikt — saturated: soaked, submerged, surrounded. It is not “created by,” “emitted from,” or “caused by.” Whatever physical-sounding vocabulary follows (force, energy, charge, weight) has to be read against this base claim, because the texts are explicit that satta itself never acts.

passages.text: 2. Satta is explicitly denied motion, pressure, and change

passages.heading: 2-satta-is-explicitly-denied-motion-pressure-and-change
passages.section: 2. Satta is explicitly denied motion, pressure, and change
passages.text: This is the texts’ own starting point for physical vocabulary — not an inference the study is making, but a direct statement, repeated in at least three of the five sources.

passages.heading: 2-satta-is-explicitly-denied-motion-pressure-and-change
passages.section: 2. Satta is explicitly denied motion, pressure, and change
passages.text: What MD says:

passages.heading: 2-satta-is-explicitly-denied-motion-pressure-and-change
passages.section: 2. Satta is explicitly denied motion, pressure, and change
passages.text: Omnipotence remains free of motion and pressure, while the whole of nature existing within it is present with motion and pressure — pressure being the compulsion toward attraction and repulsion arising under environmental (mutual) influence (SB, p. 49).

passages.heading: 2-satta-is-explicitly-denied-motion-pressure-and-change
passages.section: 2. Satta is explicitly denied motion, pressure, and change
passages.text: Consciousness/knowledge is omnipresent, permeative, transparent, and free of activity (devoid of wave or pressure); being changeless, it is not the root cause of the universe’s origin — coexistence is that root cause, and all change occurs only within nature as saturated in consciousness (MVD, p. 74).

passages.heading: 2-satta-is-explicitly-denied-motion-pressure-and-change
passages.section: 2. Satta is explicitly denied motion, pressure, and change
passages.text: Formless existence, as absolute energy, is eternally present without motion, wave, or pressure (SB, p. 50).

passages.heading: 2-satta-is-explicitly-denied-motion-pressure-and-change
passages.section: 2. Satta is explicitly denied motion, pressure, and change
passages.text: Our reading: pressure, attraction, and repulsion — the vocabulary of physical force — are placed explicitly at the level of unit-to-unit mutuality (“arising under environmental influence”), never as something satta does to a unit. This is the texts’ own firewall between the ground and physical activity.

passages.heading: 2-satta-is-explicitly-denied-motion-pressure-and-change
passages.section: 2. Satta is explicitly denied motion, pressure, and change
passages.text: 2.1 The same firewall applied to cosmogony: the Big Bang is rejected by name. JV contains the corpus’s one direct engagement with a named theory of modern cosmology, and it deploys exactly the §2 doctrine against it.

passages.heading: 2-satta-is-explicitly-denied-motion-pressure-and-change
passages.section: 2. Satta is explicitly denied motion, pressure, and change
passages.text: What MD says:

passages.heading: 2-satta-is-explicitly-denied-motion-pressure-and-change
passages.section: 2. Satta is explicitly denied motion, pressure, and change
passages.text: Omnipotence (Space) has no attribute by which it could apply a force — there are no waves, motion, or pressure in Space — so a hypothesis that the universe began with a Big Bang whose resulting force set everything in motion does not hold; every entity is instead energised, active, and inspired directly within Omnipotence (JV, p. 149).

passages.heading: 2-satta-is-explicitly-denied-motion-pressure-and-change
passages.section: 2. Satta is explicitly denied motion, pressure, and change
passages.text: Units are distinct from one another, and yet able to join with one another, because Omnipotence exists in between them; this is the basis for composition and decomposition of entities in nature (JV, p. 149).

passages.heading: 2-satta-is-explicitly-denied-motion-pressure-and-change
passages.section: 2. Satta is explicitly denied motion, pressure, and change
passages.text: Our reading: the Big Bang is not disputed on observational grounds (redshift, background radiation, etc. go unmentioned) but ruled out a priori: any cosmogonic first-force would have to be a force applied by the ground itself, and the ground is definitionally forceless. Note this sits on the same pages as the zero-attraction passage (§10.1) — in the source they are one continuous argument. Claim 2 also restates the “distance is satta” claim of SB p. 79 (§4) from the other direction: satta-in-between is simultaneously what keeps units distinct and what lets them join. This pairs with §11 below (no creation, no annihilation): the darshan’s alternative to cosmogony is not a different origin story but the denial that an origin event is needed at all — coexistence is anaadi, beginningless.

passages.section: 3. Two kinds of energy: Absolute vs. Relative
passages.text: 3. Two kinds of energy: Absolute vs. Relative

passages.heading: 3-two-kinds-of-energy-absolute-vs-relative
passages.section: 3. Two kinds of energy: Absolute vs. Relative
passages.text: MVD names this distinction directly, and it is probably the single most useful primitive for organising everything else in this note.

passages.heading: 3-two-kinds-of-energy-absolute-vs-relative
passages.section: 3. Two kinds of energy: Absolute vs. Relative
passages.text: What MD says:

passages.heading: 3-two-kinds-of-energy-absolute-vs-relative
passages.section: 3. Two kinds of energy: Absolute vs. Relative
passages.text: Relative energy (sapeksh oorja) is the power that does not become apparent without the mutuality of units — pressure, waves, and fields among physical/chemical entities, and also heat, sound, and electricity, are all named as relative energy (MVD, p. 40).

passages.heading: 3-two-kinds-of-energy-absolute-vs-relative
passages.section: 3. Two kinds of energy: Absolute vs. Relative
passages.text: Absolute and relative energy are mutually necessary: without absolute energy there is no basic impulsion in matter, and without matter absolute energy is not revealed; nature is eternally present in absolute energy (MVD, p. 40).

passages.heading: 3-two-kinds-of-energy-absolute-vs-relative
passages.section: 3. Two kinds of energy: Absolute vs. Relative
passages.text: The entire material universe — its state and its motion alike — is saturated within and contained by absolute energy (MVD, p. 45).

passages.heading: 3-two-kinds-of-energy-absolute-vs-relative
passages.section: 3. Two kinds of energy: Absolute vs. Relative
passages.text: Our reading: Absolute energy = satta itself, as the inherent, ever-present ground — inseparable from matter but not a force acting on it. Relative energy = everything that shows up only between units: pressure, waves, fields, heat, sound, electricity. Claim 1 is the clearest single statement in the corpus for “which physical phenomena are unit–unit, and which are satta–unit”: by MVD’s own definition, every named physical force (heat, sound, electricity, pressure, waves, fields) is relative energy — i.e., strictly inter-unit. Satta’s own energy is never itself named as one of the physical forces; it is what the physical forces are various manifestations of, at one remove.

passages.heading: 4-the-saturation-bond-itself-is-described-in-force-language
passages.section: 4. The saturation bond itself is described in force language
passages.text: 4. The saturation bond itself is described in force language

passages.heading: 4-the-saturation-bond-itself-is-described-in-force-language
passages.section: 4. The saturation bond itself is described in force language
passages.text: Here is the tension worth sitting with. Section 2 above establishes that satta does not act, has no pressure, no wave, no motion. But when the texts describe what saturation does to a unit, they switch into force vocabulary — repeatedly, not as a one-off metaphor.

passages.heading: 4-the-saturation-bond-itself-is-described-in-force-language
passages.section: 4. The saturation bond itself is described in force language
passages.text: What MD says:

passages.heading: 4-the-saturation-bond-itself-is-described-in-force-language
passages.section: 4. The saturation bond itself is described in force language
passages.text: Units’ mutual recognition and regulation arise solely from their saturation and energisation in Omnipotence; this submersion is why every unit has space all around it — “being soaked itself is forcefulness” (SB, p. 57).

passages.heading: 4-the-saturation-bond-itself-is-described-in-force-language
passages.section: 4. The saturation bond itself is described in force language
passages.text: The force in a unit is essentially magnetic force, signifying its being soaked in Omnipotence; because this forcefulness runs through the unit constantly, the constancy of effort is self-evident (SB, p. 61).

passages.heading: 4-the-saturation-bond-itself-is-described-in-force-language
passages.section: 4. The saturation bond itself is described in force language
passages.text: Saturation in uniform energy is itself forcefulness; forcefulness is itself basic impulsion; basic impulsion is itself activity; activity is itself effort-motion-result; and effort-motion-result is itself development and its continuity (SB, p. 62).

passages.heading: 4-the-saturation-bond-itself-is-described-in-force-language
passages.section: 4. The saturation bond itself is described in force language
passages.text: Every existent, as a consequence of its saturation in Omnipotence, is endowed with forcefulness manifested as magnetic forcefulness — forcefulness is existentially inherent in every atomic particle (SB, p. 98).

passages.heading: 4-the-saturation-bond-itself-is-described-in-force-language
passages.section: 4. The saturation bond itself is described in force language
passages.text: Forcefulness is expressed because formful existence remains saturated in formless existence; every unit — molecules, atoms, even the particles contained within atoms — remains regulated within a definite, fixed distance from every other, and that distance is itself formless existence (SB, p. 79).

passages.heading: 4-the-saturation-bond-itself-is-described-in-force-language
passages.section: 4. The saturation bond itself is described in force language
passages.text: Every entity, from the smallest to the biggest unit, is submerged, soaked, and surrounded in the omnipresent; it is by virtue of being energy-endowed that force-endowment, and magnetic-force-endowment, is understood — it is this force by which the particles of an atom recognise one another in mutuality and participate in order (KD, p. 54; our translation).

passages.heading: 4-the-saturation-bond-itself-is-described-in-force-language
passages.section: 4. The saturation bond itself is described in force language
passages.text: Whatever we measure as distance, amid mutuality, we are measuring only the pervasive entity itself — every distance measurement is a measurement of satta (KD, pp. 125–126).

passages.heading: 4-the-saturation-bond-itself-is-described-in-force-language
passages.section: 4. The saturation bond itself is described in force language
passages.text: Our reading: the texts’ own resolution (implicit, not stated as a resolution) is that saturation is an eternal endowment, not an event — “forcefulness” names what is always-already true of a soaked unit, not a transmission that happens at a moment in time, the way one billiard ball strikes another. Claim 3’s chain (saturation → forcefulness → basic impulsion → activity → effort-motion-result) is presented as one continuous unfolding “internal” to the bond, not a causal relay between separate things. Even so, the literal choice of “magnetic force” (चुम्बकीय बल) for a bond that is also called actionless is a real interpretive knot — see §15.

passages.heading: 4-the-saturation-bond-itself-is-described-in-force-language
passages.section: 4. The saturation bond itself is described in force language
passages.text: Claim 6 grounds recognition-and-regulation (the two effects claim 1 derives from saturation) in the same endowment — so the SB and KD chains match link for link: saturation → energy-endowment → (magnetic) force-endowment → recognition → regulation/order.

passages.heading: 4-the-saturation-bond-itself-is-described-in-force-language
passages.section: 4. The saturation bond itself is described in force language
passages.text: Claim 5 (SB p. 79) is also the clearest textual basis for “distance is satta”: the gap between any two particles or units is not empty in the sense of nothing there — it is formless existence itself. Space (a name the texts also give satta — see MVD p. 40’s list: Uniform Energy, Space, Knowledge, Consciousness, Absolute Energy) is not a container satta sits inside; it is satta, seen from the side of separation between bounded things. Claim 7 (KD ch. 3.14) makes the same claim operational, extending it to measurement itself — the one place the unmeasurable ground is said to be what rulers in fact measure.

passages.heading: 5-the-five-forces-table-physics-mapped-onto-jeevans-faculties
passages.section: 5. The Five Forces table — physics mapped onto jeevan’s faculties
passages.text: 5. The Five Forces table — physics mapped onto jeevan’s faculties

passages.heading: 5-the-five-forces-table-physics-mapped-onto-jeevans-faculties
passages.section: 5. The Five Forces table — physics mapped onto jeevan’s faculties
passages.text: This is the most striking single artifact in the corpus for this question: SB contains an actual table pairing the four fundamental forces of physics, plus a fifth, against the five faculties of jeevan (SB, p. 85):

passages.heading: 5-the-five-forces-table-physics-mapped-onto-jeevans-faculties
passages.section: 5. The Five Forces table — physics mapped onto jeevan’s faculties
passages.text: Insentient Powers — The Five Forces Jeevan faculty Sentient Power Electromagnetic Force Mun Hope Gravitational Force Vritti Thought The Weak Interaction Force Chitta Visualisation The Strong Interaction Force Buddhi Resolve Mediative Force Atma Realisation

passages.heading: 5-the-five-forces-table-physics-mapped-onto-jeevans-faculties
passages.section: 5. The Five Forces table — physics mapped onto jeevan’s faculties
passages.text: What MD says:

passages.heading: 5-the-five-forces-table-physics-mapped-onto-jeevans-faculties
passages.section: 5. The Five Forces table — physics mapped onto jeevan’s faculties
passages.text: It is only in the atom that all five forces are seen to be fully operative; in post-forms — molecules and molecular compositions — the mediative force is no longer apparent, which is why the study and teaching of all five forces is accessible only through the atom (SB, p. 84).

passages.heading: 5-the-five-forces-table-physics-mapped-onto-jeevans-faculties
passages.section: 5. The Five Forces table — physics mapped onto jeevan’s faculties
passages.text: Mediative activity is the manifestation of mediative force and power, situated at the centre of the atom, continuously controlling the generative and degenerative forces; insentient powers are subject to erosion, whereas sentient powers remain inexhaustible (SB, p. 84).

passages.heading: 5-the-five-forces-table-physics-mapped-onto-jeevans-faculties
passages.section: 5. The Five Forces table — physics mapped onto jeevan’s faculties
passages.text: Our reading: the darshan takes over the standard four-force inventory of physics wholesale (electromagnetic, gravitational, weak, strong) and adds one the texts consider missing — a “mediative force” (madhyastha bal), located at the atomic nucleus, whose job is to regulate/normalise the other four (“generative and degenerative powers”). This fifth force is presented as the reason an insentient atom can, on developing, become a sentient one — mediative force is insentient nature’s structural analogue of atma. It is worth being careful in the paper about what kind of claim this is: it is not proposing a fifth force for physics to detect: it is a structural analogy (insentient force : atom :: sentient faculty : jeevan), used to argue that jeevan’s five-faculty architecture is not arbitrary but mirrors a five-fold structure the darshan already claims to see in insentient matter. Whether this is meant descriptively (physics literally has five forces once you count correctly) or analogically (a template shared across orders) is not disambiguated in the passage itself — flag as open in §15.

passages.heading: 6-atomic-structure-nucleus-orbits-and-the-absence-of-a-numbered-periodic-table
passages.section: 6. Atomic structure: nucleus, orbits, and the absence of a numbered periodic table
passages.text: 6. Atomic structure: nucleus, orbits, and the absence of a numbered periodic table

passages.heading: 6-atomic-structure-nucleus-orbits-and-the-absence-of-a-numbered-periodic-table
passages.section: 6. Atomic structure: nucleus, orbits, and the absence of a numbered periodic table
passages.text: This is the most direct material for “atomic number and orbital shells,” and it turns out to be more developed than the Five Forces table alone suggests. The darshan gives every atom — insentient or sentient — the same generic architecture: a central particle-cluster (nucleus, madhyansh) surrounded by particles arranged in concentric orbits (parivesh, literally “surroundings,” translated here as orbit/shell).

passages.heading: 6-atomic-structure-nucleus-orbits-and-the-absence-of-a-numbered-periodic-table
passages.section: 6. Atomic structure: nucleus, orbits, and the absence of a numbered periodic table
passages.text: What MD says:

passages.heading: 6-atomic-structure-nucleus-orbits-and-the-absence-of-a-numbered-periodic-table
passages.section: 6. Atomic structure: nucleus, orbits, and the absence of a numbered periodic table
passages.text: Particles in every atom are situated either in the nucleus or in the surrounding orbits; the first orbit’s one or more particles continuously revolve around the nucleus, and the same holds for the second, third, fourth, and further orbits; space pervades all around the atom and around the particles within its constitution (MVD, p. 78).

passages.heading: 6-atomic-structure-nucleus-orbits-and-the-absence-of-a-numbered-periodic-table
passages.section: 6. Atomic structure: nucleus, orbits, and the absence of a numbered periodic table
passages.text: The kind, state, and existential measure of atoms are determined by differences in the number of particles in their nucleus and their orbiting particles (MVD, p. 42).

passages.heading: 6-atomic-structure-nucleus-orbits-and-the-absence-of-a-numbered-periodic-table
passages.section: 6. Atomic structure: nucleus, orbits, and the absence of a numbered periodic table
passages.text: The basic element in the constitution of all large entities is the atom, and the constitution principle of atoms of all elements is the same — a nucleus and orbiting particles. All orders of nature arise from the activeness of particles in atoms and their position in the development progression (MVD, p. 149).

passages.heading: 6-atomic-structure-nucleus-orbits-and-the-absence-of-a-numbered-periodic-table
passages.section: 6. Atomic structure: nucleus, orbits, and the absence of a numbered periodic table
passages.text: Our reading: the darshan does have a real “shell model” — nucleus plus a variable number of concentric orbits, with particle count in each determining the atom’s “kind” (jaati), its overall size/mass, and (via distance from the nucleus) its charge state. Claim 3 states this architecture is one universal principle across all “elements” and all four orders — material, bio, animal, knowledge-order atoms are not built from different kinds of parts; they differ only in how many particles occupy which orbits and how “active” (in the effort/ascending sense) each orbit is.

passages.heading: 6-atomic-structure-nucleus-orbits-and-the-absence-of-a-numbered-periodic-table
passages.section: 6. Atomic structure: nucleus, orbits, and the absence of a numbered periodic table
passages.text: 6.1 Growth rule: how orbits and mass build up together. AVD gives the clearest statement connecting orbital structure to weight (cross-reference §10).

passages.heading: 6-atomic-structure-nucleus-orbits-and-the-absence-of-a-numbered-periodic-table
passages.section: 6. Atomic structure: nucleus, orbits, and the absence of a numbered periodic table
passages.text: What MD says:

passages.heading: 6-atomic-structure-nucleus-orbits-and-the-absence-of-a-numbered-periodic-table
passages.section: 6. Atomic structure: nucleus, orbits, and the absence of a numbered periodic table
passages.text: The atom’s constitution is a nucleus at the centre plus dependent particles at a well-defined distance, orbiting the nucleus — motion-paths (orbits) are an integral part of the atom. More particles in an atom means more orbits too; as the number of particles in orbits increases, the number of particles in the nucleus increases as well — this is how weight-bondage appears in atoms (AVD, p. 185).

passages.heading: 6-atomic-structure-nucleus-orbits-and-the-absence-of-a-numbered-periodic-table
passages.section: 6. Atomic structure: nucleus, orbits, and the absence of a numbered periodic table
passages.text: Our reading: growth is monotonic and coupled — more orbital particles requires a larger nucleus, and that pairing is explicitly what weight is (§10). This is the qualitative version of what KD sharpens into an inequality (§6.4a).

passages.heading: 6-atomic-structure-nucleus-orbits-and-the-absence-of-a-numbered-periodic-table
passages.section: 6. Atomic structure: nucleus, orbits, and the absence of a numbered periodic table
passages.text: 6.2 Orbital distance sets charge/regulation. AVD ties the same architecture to §8’s charge discussion (the ± sense — see §8’s terminology note), giving the nucleus an explicit regulatory role over the orbits.

passages.heading: 6-atomic-structure-nucleus-orbits-and-the-absence-of-a-numbered-periodic-table
passages.section: 6. Atomic structure: nucleus, orbits, and the absence of a numbered periodic table
passages.text: What MD says:

passages.heading: 6-atomic-structure-nucleus-orbits-and-the-absence-of-a-numbered-periodic-table
passages.section: 6. Atomic structure: nucleus, orbits, and the absence of a numbered periodic table
passages.text: Regulation of an atom’s generative/degenerative excess is the grandeur of its central particle: an increase or decrease in the precise distance of orbital particles from the nucleus is what “generative” or “degenerative” names, and this is kept in equilibrium by the strength and power of the nucleus (AVD, p. 103).

passages.heading: 6-atomic-structure-nucleus-orbits-and-the-absence-of-a-numbered-periodic-table
passages.section: 6. Atomic structure: nucleus, orbits, and the absence of a numbered periodic table
passages.text: Our reading: this is the same distance-from-nucleus definition of generative/degenerative excitation that reappears independently in §8 — a case of AVD and SB converging on the same mechanism without cross-reference.

passages.heading: 6-atomic-structure-nucleus-orbits-and-the-absence-of-a-numbered-periodic-table
passages.section: 6. Atomic structure: nucleus, orbits, and the absence of a numbered periodic table
passages.text: 6.3 Differential activity of orbits, order by order. MVD states that which orbits are “active” differs systematically by order of nature — this is as close as the texts come to something like an electron-configuration rule.

passages.heading: 6-atomic-structure-nucleus-orbits-and-the-absence-of-a-numbered-periodic-table
passages.section: 6. Atomic structure: nucleus, orbits, and the absence of a numbered periodic table
passages.text: What MD says:

passages.heading: 6-atomic-structure-nucleus-orbits-and-the-absence-of-a-numbered-periodic-table
passages.section: 6. Atomic structure: nucleus, orbits, and the absence of a numbered periodic table
passages.text: Only the particles in the last orbit of all kinds of atoms within the material order are active through effort; only the outermost and second-to-last orbits of insentient atoms are actively engaged in compounding activities; particles in the fourth, third, and second orbits in the sentient atom (animal order) are partially active; in the knowledge order, jeevan expresses four-and-a-half activities, with activeness in the fourth, third, and second orbits (MVD, pp. 78–79).

passages.heading: 6-atomic-structure-nucleus-orbits-and-the-absence-of-a-numbered-periodic-table
passages.section: 6. Atomic structure: nucleus, orbits, and the absence of a numbered periodic table
passages.text: Our reading: this is the darshan’s nearest analogue to an electron-configuration/valence-shell rule — which orbit is “doing the work” changes systematically as one moves up through the four orders of nature, without the underlying nucleus-plus-orbits architecture changing at all (§6, claim 3).

passages.heading: 6-atomic-structure-nucleus-orbits-and-the-absence-of-a-numbered-periodic-table
passages.section: 6. Atomic structure: nucleus, orbits, and the absence of a numbered periodic table
passages.text: 6.4 The one case with a fully named orbital model: jeevan itself. When the “atom” in question is a constitutionally complete, sentient one, the nucleus and its four orbits get specific names and a fixed activity count — the clearest “shell diagram” anywhere in the corpus.

passages.text: Atma, as jeevan’s nucleus, has exactly two activities — realisation (anubhav) and authenticity (pramanikta). Buddhi’s first orbit has two activities — enlightenment (bodh) and resolve (sankalp). Chitta’s second orbit — contemplation (chintan) and visualisation (chitran). Vritti’s third orbit — deliberation (tulan) and analysis (vishleshan). Mun’s fourth orbit — taste (asvadan) and selection (chayan). Together these are jeevan’s ten activities (JV, p. 92).

Radioactivity (§9.2’s excited, overfull atoms shedding internally) is then a special case of visthāpan.

passages.text: Our reading: three states, not four — plasma never appears as a state of matter anywhere in the corpus (the word occurs once in SB, p. 204, as a translation of rasa in the seven bodily dhatus). Claim 2’s “elemental = a homogeneous group of atoms” is the closest the corpus comes to defining a chemical element, and it is consistent with §6’s picture: an element is a population of same-kind atoms (same particle count), not an entry in a numbered table. One quirk worth preserving: claim 3 gives physical entities only solid and gaseous forms, reserving the full solid–liquid–gas triple for chemical substances — liquidity is apparently treated as evidence of chemical (rasa-yielding) activity, which coheres with claim 5’s claim that biological cells emerge from solidification processes of chemical entities.

passages.heading: 6-atomic-structure-nucleus-orbits-and-the-absence-of-a-numbered-periodic-table
passages.section: 6. Atomic structure: nucleus, orbits, and the absence of a numbered periodic table
passages.text: What is not there: none of the six texts assign a specific particle count to a specific named element (hydrogen, oxygen, iron, gold, etc. all appear only as generic illustrations of “-ness,” e.g. “ironness,” never with a stated number of nucleus/orbit particles) — so there is no periodic table proper, no per-element atomic-number assignments, and no electron/proton/neutron vocabulary anywhere in this corpus (verified for KD as well: no Devanagari loan-words for electron, proton, or neutron occur). §6.4a claim 4 does, however, explicitly acknowledge the element inventory as a human claim, so the darshan is aware of, and accepts the reality behind, a discrete numbered series of atomic kinds; what it declines to reproduce is the table’s contents. What exists instead is the growth law (more particles → more orbits → bigger nucleus → more weight → different “kind”), now sharpened by KD’s constraints (§6.4a: minimum 1+1 constitution; nucleus ≥ orbit count; four-orbit equilibrium) — still without the per-element numbers that would let you look up carbon’s structure the way you would in a chemistry textbook.

passages.text: Our reading: a lone ansh is not pictured as a stable, self-sufficient little sphere. Its natural condition in isolation is restlessness and incompleteness — motion without settlement — and this restlessness is itself what drives combination. This is the same restlessness-until-completion logic that KD’s “hungry”/”undigested”/”satisfied” vocabulary (§6.4b) applies at the atom level, already present in miniature at the level of a single particle — combination-seeking is not imposed on an ansh from outside; it is what the particle’s own incompleteness already drives it toward.

passages.text: Our reading: two further limits are worth making explicit, neither of which the texts state as a single claim but both of which follow from material already cited: (a) sentience/insentience is a status of the completed atom, never of an isolated particle — when an atom crosses into constitutional completeness, every particle it comprises participates in the transition equally, with no suggestion that some particles are “already” sentient ahead of others; (b) no intrinsic, standalone, measurable property (shape, size, a charge value) is ever assigned to a particle considered alone — weight, charge, and an atom’s hungry/undigested/satisfied condition (§6.4b) are all explicitly relational, a function of an ansh’s position and count relative to the others in its constitution (§§8, 10), consistent with the corpus’s general “relative energy” doctrine (§3) that named physical quantities are apparent only in mutuality. A lone ansh, by the texts’ own logic, is restless and incomplete (§6.8) but not further quantifiable until it is in relation to at least one other particle.

passages.heading: 7-motion-rotational-orbital-vibrational-and-excited-sb-charged-vs-natural-state-motion
passages.section: 7. Motion: rotational, orbital, vibrational — and “excited” (SB: “charged”) vs. “natural-state” motion
passages.text: Our reading: the darshan’s basic kinematics is: every unit (atomic or otherwise) always has rotational + orbital + vibrational motion, intrinsically (this is closer to “zero-point” activity than to Newtonian rest). What varies is whether that motion stays in its natural state (swabhav gati) or becomes excited motion (aveshit gati) under pressure from environment/naturalness — i.e., external interference is what turns ordinary intrinsic motion into excited, disturbed motion. This maps fairly directly onto §8 below (excitation), and the “orbital” component maps onto §6’s shell structure.

passages.text: Our reading: bal (force) is what a unit has by virtue of being (its endowed, standing side — §4’s saturation-forcefulness); shakti (power) is what becomes evident when it is active or in motion (the expressed, relational side — §3’s relative energy). The pair maps onto sthiti/gati exactly as absolute/relative energy maps onto satta/mutuality. Claim 2 is the corpus’s most precise indictment of physics in physics’ own terms: its instruments and formalisms only ever register excited motion (disturbances, differences, §8 — SB’s “charged motion”), so its inventory of forces omits whatever holds in the natural state — which is where the darshan locates the mediative. Claim 4 closes the definitional circle from the heat side: the unexcited state is simultaneously the thermally ordinary one.

passages.text: Activeness itself is recognised as generative, degenerative, and mediative powers; generative and degenerative powers are observed as the charge in mutuality, while the function of mediative activity is to normalise this charge — this mediative power is commonly known as the hidden energy (SB, p. 70).

passages.heading: 8-charge-and-excitation-āvesh-generativedegenerative-powers-the-nucleus-and-hidden-energy
passages.section: 8. Charge and excitation (āvesh): generative/degenerative powers, the nucleus, and “hidden energy”
passages.text: A physicochemical atom’s positive or negative charge refers to the increase or decrease of orbital particles’ distance from the nucleus; positive and negative charge are only ever relative — “more” and “less” — never complete, and for that reason never stable, so mediative power works continuously to normalise them, because the goal of mediative activity is completeness (SB, p. 70).

passages.heading: 8-charge-and-excitation-āvesh-generativedegenerative-powers-the-nucleus-and-hidden-energy
passages.section: 8. Charge and excitation (āvesh): generative/degenerative powers, the nucleus, and “hidden energy”
passages.text: (Same distance-from-nucleus definition of generative/degenerative excitation appears independently in AVD, p. 103 — see §6.2.)

passages.heading: 8-charge-and-excitation-āvesh-generativedegenerative-powers-the-nucleus-and-hidden-energy
passages.section: 8. Charge and excitation (āvesh): generative/degenerative powers, the nucleus, and “hidden energy”
passages.text: In the regulated state there is no charge — this itself is the natural state; in the charged state, the possibility of decline naturally remains inherent, and decline is itself the evidence of charge (SB, p. 79).

passages.heading: 8-charge-and-excitation-āvesh-generativedegenerative-powers-the-nucleus-and-hidden-energy
passages.section: 8. Charge and excitation (āvesh): generative/degenerative powers, the nucleus, and “hidden energy”
passages.text: Degenerative charge is always a manifestation of a problem (SB, p. 88).

passages.heading: 8-charge-and-excitation-āvesh-generativedegenerative-powers-the-nucleus-and-hidden-energy
passages.section: 8. Charge and excitation (āvesh): generative/degenerative powers, the nucleus, and “hidden energy”
passages.text: An object that has become more excited is always heated — its temperature rises (KD, p. 74; cf. SB p. 252’s heat = excitation, §9).

passages.heading: 8-charge-and-excitation-āvesh-generativedegenerative-powers-the-nucleus-and-hidden-energy
passages.section: 8. Charge and excitation (āvesh): generative/degenerative powers, the nucleus, and “hidden energy”
passages.text: An atom must already be excited before it can shed a particle (KD, p. 57; §6.4b).

passages.heading: 8-charge-and-excitation-āvesh-generativedegenerative-powers-the-nucleus-and-hidden-energy
passages.section: 8. Charge and excitation (āvesh): generative/degenerative powers, the nucleus, and “hidden energy”
passages.text: Pressure (dabāv) is the compulsion received for generative-degenerative (sam–viṣam) excitation, as distinct from natural-state motion (KD, p. 118) — folding SB p. 49’s pressure definition (§2) explicitly into excitation vocabulary.

passages.heading: 8-charge-and-excitation-āvesh-generativedegenerative-powers-the-nucleus-and-hidden-energy
passages.section: 8. Charge and excitation (āvesh): generative/degenerative powers, the nucleus, and “hidden energy”
passages.text: If the distance of an orbital particle from the nucleus increases beyond the definite good distance, the nucleus’s mediating activity applies its force and draws the particle back in; if a particle begins to approach the nucleus too closely, the nucleus likewise applies its force and fixes it back at the good distance — this two-way restoring action is the atom’s control activity (KD, p. 103).

passages.heading: 8-charge-and-excitation-āvesh-generativedegenerative-powers-the-nucleus-and-hidden-energy
passages.section: 8. Charge and excitation (āvesh): generative/degenerative powers, the nucleus, and “hidden energy”
passages.text: Every excitation works toward natural-state motion; natural-state motion works toward development progression; development progression works toward evidencing development; development works toward evidencing awakening progression; and awakening progression works toward evidencing the continuity of awakening (KD, p. 77).

passages.heading: 8-charge-and-excitation-āvesh-generativedegenerative-powers-the-nucleus-and-hidden-energy
passages.section: 8. Charge and excitation (āvesh): generative/degenerative powers, the nucleus, and “hidden energy”
passages.text: Terminology note: the Hindi root āvesh/āveshit is used contextually in the texts, and the translation must follow the context. (a) The ± sense: where the text speaks of the positive–negative (धन-ऋणात्मक) imbalance of atoms — defined by orbital particles’ distance from the nucleus (claim 2; SB p. 250: “possible to measure positive and negative charges”) — āvesh is charge, in the electric-charge sense. (b) The state sense: where the text contrasts a unit’s neutral/natural state with a disturbed one — āveshit gati vs swabhav gati (§7), an overfull atom’s condition before expelling particles (SB pp. 72, 99, 259), a heated body’s internal condition (SB p. 252) — āveshit is excited, and āvesh excitation. SB’s published English uses “charge/charged” for both senses, but glosses the state sense itself at p. 257: “entities are in a natural state or in an excited (charged) state.” MD-Mapping encodes both readings (आवेश = “agitation, charge, excitement”; आवेशित गति = “agitated state, excited state”), and its Hindi definition of āvesh is explicitly value-laden — “deluded conduct-tendency; interference, motion toward decline.” This note and the KD-Karm-Darshan-English translations apply the contextual rule in their own voice; verbatim SB quotations elsewhere in this note keep the published wording. This settles, from the vocabulary side, what this section’s reading argues from the content side: “charge” in the darshan names an imbalance-state, not an electrical quantity — and MD-Mapping’s “motion toward decline” definition is precisely claim 4’s “in the charged state, the possibility of decline naturally remains inherent.”

passages.heading: 8-charge-and-excitation-āvesh-generativedegenerative-powers-the-nucleus-and-hidden-energy
passages.section: 8. Charge and excitation (āvesh): generative/degenerative powers, the nucleus, and “hidden energy”
passages.text: Our reading: the two senses of āvesh are systematically linked in SB’s doctrine. In the ± sense, charge names the atom’s generative/degenerative imbalance — generative power in excess of degenerative, or vice versa, measured by orbital distance from the mediative reference point at the nucleus (claim 2). Positive and negative charge are explicitly called relative — a matter of “more or less” around a mean, never an absolute or stable quantity — and mediative force’s job is continuously pulling any excess back toward balance (claim 9 gives this a fully two-directional dynamical form — a restoring influence toward a set-point separation, against displacement in either direction; see §14.3 for what this does to the mediative-as-primitive claim). An atom carrying such an imbalance is thereby in the excited state — the state sense: the natural, unexcited state is definitionally the regulated (charge-free) one, and being excited is already partway toward decline. So the ontology runs: ± charge (imbalance) → excited state (disturbed condition) → decline, unless the mediative normalises it. This is a value-laden physics: excitation is functionally close to what SB elsewhere calls “problem,” and its absence is close to what it calls “resolution” (samadhan) — consistent with the book’s title. Claim 10 embeds excitation in a universal directional chain; de-excitation is thus not merely local relaxation but the first step of a cosmic monotone — the darshan’s arrow of change (taken up in §14.3).

passages.heading: 9-heat-magnetism-electricity-radiation
passages.section: 9. Heat, magnetism, electricity, radiation
passages.text: 9. Heat, magnetism, electricity, radiation

passages.heading: 9-heat-magnetism-electricity-radiation
passages.section: 9. Heat, magnetism, electricity, radiation
passages.text: What MD says:

passages.heading: 9-heat-magnetism-electricity-radiation
passages.section: 9. Heat, magnetism, electricity, radiation
passages.text: Radiance and imaging are not forms of motion or pressure; nevertheless, the intrinsic properties inherent in every entity exert influence on one another — heat, magnetism, electricity, and weight influence one another, and this field of influence is itself part of their grandeur (SB, p. 252).

passages.heading: 9-heat-magnetism-electricity-radiation
passages.section: 9. Heat, magnetism, electricity, radiation
passages.text: Heat, magnetism, and electrical effects are projected on this same basis; fundamentally, heat equals the charge of a unit — the greater the internal charge within a planetary body, the more it tends to transform into atomic species of progressively lower numerical constitution (SB, p. 252).

passages.heading: 9-heat-magnetism-electricity-radiation
passages.section: 9. Heat, magnetism, electricity, radiation
passages.text: Biological cells’ mutual coordination and harmony is manifested through pulsation — contraction and expansion operating respectively as pressure and wave — and the entire biological-order unit is thereby proven to be electrically receptive (SB, p. 83).

passages.heading: 9-heat-magnetism-electricity-radiation
passages.section: 9. Heat, magnetism, electricity, radiation
passages.text: Applying magnetic force to an atom generates a charge within it, leading to disintegration of its components; this reveals that the disintegrating force — electromagnetic force — is external to the atom itself, interacting with and altering its natural state (SB, p. 128).

passages.heading: 9-heat-magnetism-electricity-radiation
passages.section: 9. Heat, magnetism, electricity, radiation
passages.text: Humans came to recognise the natural phenomenon of electricity through natural correlation, imaginativeness, and freedom of action, having already identified magnetic elements from prior events, which established the tradition of studying magnetism (SB, p. 128).

passages.heading: 9-heat-magnetism-electricity-radiation
passages.section: 9. Heat, magnetism, electricity, radiation
passages.text: Our reading: heat, magnetism, electricity, and weight are grouped together explicitly as one family — properties that “influence one another” through a “field of influence,” and are explicitly not forms of motion or pressure in themselves (they are effects of the underlying excitation/pressure dynamics, not identical to them). Heat is given a specific reductive definition: heat = excitation (claim 2). Claim 4’s critique of experimental particle physics is philosophical, not technical: it reads magnetic/electromagnetic manipulation of atoms as an externally imposed distortion, and contrasts this with the darshan’s preferred method of studying wholes without destroying them (a recurring methodological theme — see also §6.4.2 of The Ontology of Coexistence on evidence standards).

passages.heading: 9-heat-magnetism-electricity-radiation
passages.section: 9. Heat, magnetism, electricity, radiation
passages.text: 9.1 The Sun, excess heat, and the “law of complementariness.” Directly following the heat = excitation passage, SB gives its one worked cosmological-scale application of the excitation doctrine.

passages.heading: 9-heat-magnetism-electricity-radiation
passages.section: 9. Heat, magnetism, electricity, radiation
passages.text: What MD says:

passages.heading: 9-heat-magnetism-electricity-radiation
passages.section: 9. Heat, magnetism, electricity, radiation
passages.text: A heated object (e.g. the Sun) reaches its natural state according to development progression; until such a state is established, the entire environment — including the Earth and other planets of comparatively lower temperature — distributes among itself the excess heat projected from the Sun, so that the Sun can become free from its excess heat through the law of complementariness (SB, p. 252).

passages.heading: 9-heat-magnetism-electricity-radiation
passages.section: 9. Heat, magnetism, electricity, radiation
passages.text: Our reading: see §9.2’s synthesis below — the Sun’s cooling is read as approach to its natural state, not fuel consumption.

passages.heading: 9-heat-magnetism-electricity-radiation
passages.section: 9. Heat, magnetism, electricity, radiation
passages.text: 9.2 Radioactivity: “overfull” atoms and internally deployed heat. SB has an explicit account of radioactivity and nuclear explosion, entirely in the vocabulary of §6 (particle counts) and §8 (excitation and mediative regulation).

passages.heading: 9-heat-magnetism-electricity-radiation
passages.section: 9. Heat, magnetism, electricity, radiation
passages.text: What MD says:

passages.heading: 9-heat-magnetism-electricity-radiation
passages.section: 9. Heat, magnetism, electricity, radiation
passages.text: Atoms that have become overfull are radioactive by nature; radioactive substances are defined by intrinsic atomic heat or fire beginning to deploy internally — in an excited or interfered state, the pressure of this internalised heat may increase to the point of an explosive condition, and on this basis it appears reasonable to infer that in the Sun, the maximum number of overfull atoms have become charged, resulting in continuous nuclear explosions (SB, p. 259).

passages.heading: 9-heat-magnetism-electricity-radiation
passages.section: 9. Heat, magnetism, electricity, radiation
passages.text: Human-triggered explosions occur because extracting substances that function beneath the Earth’s surface (per the law of complementariness) interferes with the nucleus’s naturally mediative activity — mediative force and power become incapable of balancing the charged components, leading to explosions (SB, p. 258).

passages.heading: 9-heat-magnetism-electricity-radiation
passages.section: 9. Heat, magnetism, electricity, radiation
passages.text: Our reading: this closes a loop the earlier sections leave open. §6’s growth rule said more particles → more orbits → bigger nucleus; here we get the failure mode of that progression: an atom can become overfull, at which point the mediative force can no longer normalise its generative/degenerative excitations and the excess deploys internally as heat — radioactivity. The Sun is then read not as a fusion reactor but as a vast population of overfull, excited atoms in continuous explosion, whose excess heat the cooler planets absorb (§9.1) until the Sun too reaches its natural state. Radioactive decay, solar output, and nuclear weapons are thus one phenomenon at three scales, and all three are excited states — i.e., in SB’s value-laden register (§8), problems awaiting resolution. Note the direction of explanation is the reverse of standard astrophysics: the Sun is cooling toward its natural state, not burning through fuel.

passages.heading: 9-heat-magnetism-electricity-radiation
passages.section: 9. Heat, magnetism, electricity, radiation
passages.text: 9.3 The critique extended: quantum mechanics, relativity, and fission. AVD broadens SB p. 128’s methodological complaint into a survey of physics’ own self-descriptions.

passages.heading: 9-heat-magnetism-electricity-radiation
passages.section: 9. Heat, magnetism, electricity, radiation
passages.text: What MD says:

passages.heading: 9-heat-magnetism-electricity-radiation
passages.section: 9. Heat, magnetism, electricity, radiation
passages.text: Specialisation has come to a purposeless dead end in all disciplines — quantum mechanics, for example, is facing the dead end of instability-uncertainty (AVD, pp. 63–64).

passages.heading: 9-heat-magnetism-electricity-radiation
passages.section: 9. Heat, magnetism, electricity, radiation
passages.text: Relativity specialists use imagination to explain phenomena not completely understood so far — e.g. converting a magnetic field into electric current usable as work energy — and experiments are still being conducted to conclude whether waves should be categorised as made up of particles, with uncertainty still looming on the question (AVD, p. 64; the translator inserts a bracketed “From internet:” gloss on wave–particle duality at this point — a translator’s addition, not source text).

passages.heading: 9-heat-magnetism-electricity-radiation
passages.section: 9. Heat, magnetism, electricity, radiation
passages.text: Nuclear fission — the splitting of the atom — was arrived at by a mathematical approach, discovered for making increasingly more powerful nuclear bombs (JV, p. 119).

passages.heading: 9-heat-magnetism-electricity-radiation
passages.section: 9. Heat, magnetism, electricity, radiation
passages.text: Our reading: the corpus’s engagement with named modern physics is thus wider than SB p. 128 alone: Big Bang cosmology (§2.1), quantum mechanics and wave–particle duality, relativity, and fission are all addressed by name, and always with the same two-pronged objection — epistemic (uncertainty/instability as a dead end, not a finding) and moral (fragmentation-by-force as destruction, fission as bomb-making). Nowhere is the mathematics engaged on its own terms; the objection is to the method and its motive, consistent with SB’s own aphorism that mathematics is more than the eyes and less than understanding (SB, p. 87).

passages.heading: 9-heat-magnetism-electricity-radiation
passages.section: 9. Heat, magnetism, electricity, radiation
passages.text: 9.4 KD’s heat mechanics, waves, electricity, and celestial order. KD ch. 3.7 (“Heat and the Earth’s Balance”) and ch. 3.13 (“Pressure, Flow, Wave, Electromagnetic Force”) contain the corpus’s most worked-out phenomenal physics (all quotes our translation).

passages.heading: 9-heat-magnetism-electricity-radiation
passages.section: 9. Heat, magnetism, electricity, radiation
passages.text: What MD says:

passages.heading: 9-heat-magnetism-electricity-radiation
passages.section: 9. Heat, magnetism, electricity, radiation
passages.text: Heat only reflects (parāvartit) from a region of greater heat toward an adjacent region of lesser heat; heat spreads by molecules near the source becoming hot and expanding, passing heat molecule-to-molecule until everything arrives at normal temperature, which means being in natural-state motion (KD, p. 75).

passages.heading: 9-heat-magnetism-electricity-radiation
passages.section: 9. Heat, magnetism, electricity, radiation
passages.text: Solids expand when heat is introduced, becoming liquid, then rarefied; heated iron keeps reflecting heat until it has cooled, distributing its heat among all associated substances (KD, p. 74).

passages.heading: 9-heat-magnetism-electricity-radiation
passages.section: 9. Heat, magnetism, electricity, radiation
passages.text: Waves occur differently by state of matter: in solid objects, waves are vibrational motion; in liquid, waves are the reaction produced by contact of air or objects; in rarefied substance, sound, heat, electricity, ray, and radiation are evidenced in wave form (KD, p. 118).

passages.heading: 9-heat-magnetism-electricity-radiation
passages.section: 9. Heat, magnetism, electricity, radiation
passages.text: Sound arises from the friction or collision of one or more objects (two stones rubbed, metals struck, leaves in wind); word-waves travel by pressure imposed on the atmosphere’s molecular groups, transmitted molecule to molecule across distance — radio and television waves are held to be word and sound propagated electricity-borne (KD, pp. 118–119).

passages.heading: 9-heat-magnetism-electricity-radiation
passages.section: 9. Heat, magnetism, electricity, radiation
passages.text: An electric wave is the flow produced by the fragmentation (vikhaṇḍan) of magnetic current; the fragments into which magnetic current is broken are transmitted through a medium, and the whole of nature is found to be electricity-receptive, at minimum or maximum, with the degree settled by pressure, flow, and quantity (KD, p. 118).

passages.heading: 9-heat-magnetism-electricity-radiation
passages.section: 9. Heat, magnetism, electricity, radiation
passages.text: Lightning is this electromagnetic wave occurring naturally; thunder is the sound of dense clouds nearing one another from their “good distance,” and when they connect with the Earth, electric flow runs of itself; the dynamo obtains light by the same fragmentation-of-magnetic-current method, rotated mechanically (KD, p. 119).

passages.heading: 9-heat-magnetism-electricity-radiation
passages.section: 9. Heat, magnetism, electricity, radiation
passages.text: The Sun’s heat is reflected equally in all directions; the Earth-facing side becomes hot, producing sunrise/sunset and the day’s temperature curve. The Earth’s rotation presents its faces to the Sun in turn; its revolution around the Sun, maintaining a “good distance” (acchī dūrī) along with all the planet-spheres of the solar array, follows an elliptical (aṇḍākār), not fully circular, path, whose chief intent is the Earth’s self-organised tendency of seasonal change (ṛtu parivartan) (KD, p. 76).

passages.heading: 9-heat-magnetism-electricity-radiation
passages.section: 9. Heat, magnetism, electricity, radiation
passages.text: The Sun is in the ultimate condition of decline, destined in the course of time to enter development progression (KD, p. 77).

passages.heading: 9-heat-magnetism-electricity-radiation
passages.section: 9. Heat, magnetism, electricity, radiation
passages.text: Heat transfer generalises to astronomy: planet-orbs of maximum heat — such as the Sun’s — have that heat absorbed into all facing planet-orbs in which less heat remains (KD, pp. 77–78).

passages.heading: 9-heat-magnetism-electricity-radiation
passages.section: 9. Heat, magnetism, electricity, radiation
passages.text: The Earth’s pole-to-pole magnetic current is what keeps the planet solid; if overheating deflected that current, the Earth would begin to scatter (KD, p. 81).

passages.heading: 9-heat-magnetism-electricity-radiation
passages.section: 9. Heat, magnetism, electricity, radiation
passages.text: Our reading: three things stand out. First, the direction of KD’s explanations: heat flows hot→cold not as statistics but as mutual “recognition–fulfilment” between substances (claim 2’s melting iron “accepts” deployed heat — KD explicitly calls this acceptance recognition, extending §4’s recognition doctrine into thermodynamics). Second, magnetism is treated as prior to electricity (claim 5: electricity = fragmented magnetic current) — the exact inverse of the electromagnetic hierarchy, but consistent with the corpus’s decision to make “magnetic forcefulness” the fundamental endowment (§4). Third, the celestial mechanics (claim 7) is teleological: elliptical orbits and maintained “good distance” are not consequences of gravitation but expressions of order whose purpose is seasons, and ultimately the development-progression toward jagriti on Earth. Note the ellipse itself is correctly asserted — what differs from Kepler is the direction of explanation, the same pattern as §9.2’s Sun. Claim 8 is the strongest single confirmation of §9.2’s cooling-Sun reading; claim 9 is KD’s version of SB p. 252’s law of complementariness (§9.1); claim 10 gives magnetism, again, the structurally prior, binding role (cf. §4). One caution for the paper: KD ch. 3.12 shows parāvartan–pratyāvartan (reflection–projection, per the project’s settled rendering) to be a fully general category — teaching/study, evidence-giving, and heat transfer are all its species — so ch. 3.7’s thermal “reflection” (claim 1) should not be read as a specifically optical or thermodynamic technical term.
