passages.text: 10. Mass and weight: the most concrete explanatory chain in the corpus

passages.heading: 10-mass-and-weight-the-most-concrete-explanatory-chain-in-the-corpus
passages.section: 10. Mass and weight: the most concrete explanatory chain in the corpus
passages.text: This is the best-developed physics-adjacent explanation in the primary texts, and it directly answers “how do atoms get weight/mass.”

passages.heading: 10-mass-and-weight-the-most-concrete-explanatory-chain-in-the-corpus
passages.section: 10. Mass and weight: the most concrete explanatory chain in the corpus
passages.text: 10.1 The ground state is weightless. JV, in Q&A form, states this as an axiom.

passages.heading: 10-mass-and-weight-the-most-concrete-explanatory-chain-in-the-corpus
passages.section: 10. Mass and weight: the most concrete explanatory chain in the corpus
passages.text: What MD says:

passages.heading: 10-mass-and-weight-the-most-concrete-explanatory-chain-in-the-corpus
passages.section: 10. Mass and weight: the most concrete explanatory chain in the corpus
passages.text: Materialism holds that units, by displacing space, are mightier (heavier) than space; but in reality all units — Earth, Sun, solar systems, and galaxies — exist in a state of zero-attraction, the absolute state, meaning there is no weight in the coexistence of Omnipotence and units. Weight becomes evident only in the interaction of units — for example, in the mutuality of two atoms due to their tendency to form a molecule, or among molecules due to their tendency to form definite compositions. This manifestation of weight in the mutuality of units is what is commonly called the gravitational force (JV, pp. 149–150).

passages.heading: 10-mass-and-weight-the-most-concrete-explanatory-chain-in-the-corpus
passages.section: 10. Mass and weight: the most concrete explanatory chain in the corpus
passages.text: Our reading: weight is defined out of the ground state entirely and relocated to the tendency of units to combine — this is the axiom the rest of §10 builds on.

passages.heading: 10-mass-and-weight-the-most-concrete-explanatory-chain-in-the-corpus
passages.section: 10. Mass and weight: the most concrete explanatory chain in the corpus
passages.text: 10.2 Three attraction-states, and a derivation chain for weight.

passages.heading: 10-mass-and-weight-the-most-concrete-explanatory-chain-in-the-corpus
passages.section: 10. Mass and weight: the most concrete explanatory chain in the corpus
passages.text: What MD says:

passages.heading: 10-mass-and-weight-the-most-concrete-explanatory-chain-in-the-corpus
passages.section: 10. Mass and weight: the most concrete explanatory chain in the corpus
passages.text: Every planet is in a state of zero attraction in space, its position determined by its motion; units in a state of positive-attraction are attracted to something, units in a state of negative-attraction attract something, and units in the zero-attraction state are independent (MVD, p. 45).

passages.heading: 10-mass-and-weight-the-most-concrete-explanatory-chain-in-the-corpus
passages.section: 10. Mass and weight: the most concrete explanatory chain in the corpus
passages.text: Weight depends on attraction; attraction depends on mutuality; mutuality depends on relative smallness or bigness; smallness or bigness depends on composition and relative energies; composition and relative energies depend on activity; activity depends on matter; and matter’s development or decline depends on the right-use or misuse of relative energy (MVD, p. 45).

passages.heading: 10-mass-and-weight-the-most-concrete-explanatory-chain-in-the-corpus
passages.section: 10. Mass and weight: the most concrete explanatory chain in the corpus
passages.text: Our reading: the dependency chain in claim 2 traces weight backward through attraction → mutuality → relative size (laghuta/guruta, the same root that gives gurutvakarshan, the ordinary Hindi word for gravitation, so the etymology is doing real work here) → composition/relative-energy → activity → matter itself, terminating in “right-use or misuse of relative energy” — i.e., ultimately a normative rather than a purely mechanical vocabulary.

passages.heading: 10-mass-and-weight-the-most-concrete-explanatory-chain-in-the-corpus
passages.section: 10. Mass and weight: the most concrete explanatory chain in the corpus
passages.text: 10.3 Atomic mass = particle count. (Same principle as §6’s orbit/nucleus growth rule, restated directly in terms of mass.)

passages.heading: 10-mass-and-weight-the-most-concrete-explanatory-chain-in-the-corpus
passages.section: 10. Mass and weight: the most concrete explanatory chain in the corpus
passages.text: What MD says:

passages.heading: 10-mass-and-weight-the-most-concrete-explanatory-chain-in-the-corpus
passages.section: 10. Mass and weight: the most concrete explanatory chain in the corpus
passages.text: The mass and lineage (or category) of atoms is determined by the number of their constituent particles; further development follows the principle of coexistence, with a two-particle atom being the simplest case (SB, p. 182).

passages.heading: 10-mass-and-weight-the-most-concrete-explanatory-chain-in-the-corpus
passages.section: 10. Mass and weight: the most concrete explanatory chain in the corpus
passages.text: The atom is established as the basic quantum: since molecules and molecular forms arise from atoms, understanding the atom as the fundamental unit of measurement provides the key to comprehending the quantity of all bodies (SB, p. 86).

passages.heading: 10-mass-and-weight-the-most-concrete-explanatory-chain-in-the-corpus
passages.section: 10. Mass and weight: the most concrete explanatory chain in the corpus
passages.text: More particles in an atom means more orbits also; as orbital particles increase, nucleus particles increase too — this is how weight-bondage appears in atoms (AVD, p. 185; see §6.1).

passages.heading: 10-mass-and-weight-the-most-concrete-explanatory-chain-in-the-corpus
passages.section: 10. Mass and weight: the most concrete explanatory chain in the corpus
passages.text: Our reading: atomic mass proper is simpler and more concrete than gravitation/weight (§10.1–10.2): it is just the count of constituent particles in an atom (nucleus + orbits, §6), which is also what fixes which “species” (element-analogue) the atom belongs to.

passages.heading: 10-mass-and-weight-the-most-concrete-explanatory-chain-in-the-corpus
passages.section: 10. Mass and weight: the most concrete explanatory chain in the corpus
passages.text: 10.4 Sentience is explicitly freedom from weight.

passages.heading: 10-mass-and-weight-the-most-concrete-explanatory-chain-in-the-corpus
passages.section: 10. Mass and weight: the most concrete explanatory chain in the corpus
passages.text: What MD says:

passages.heading: 10-mass-and-weight-the-most-concrete-explanatory-chain-in-the-corpus
passages.section: 10. Mass and weight: the most concrete explanatory chain in the corpus
passages.text: Every sentient unit, i.e. jeevan, is free from weight-bondage and molecular-bondage (SB, p. 114).

passages.heading: 10-mass-and-weight-the-most-concrete-explanatory-chain-in-the-corpus
passages.section: 10. Mass and weight: the most concrete explanatory chain in the corpus
passages.text: A constitutionally complete atom is free from molecular and gravitational bonds, and this itself is its grandeur (JV, p. 150).

passages.heading: 10-mass-and-weight-the-most-concrete-explanatory-chain-in-the-corpus
passages.section: 10. Mass and weight: the most concrete explanatory chain in the corpus
passages.text: Our reading: the clean, repeated corollary of §§10.1–10.3 is that a jeevan atom (constitutionally complete, sentient) is explicitly exempted from both molecular bonding and gravitational/weight bonding — weight is presented as strictly a feature of insentient nature’s combinatorial tendency, one of the things a unit “graduates out of” at the sentience threshold.

passages.heading: 10-mass-and-weight-the-most-concrete-explanatory-chain-in-the-corpus
passages.section: 10. Mass and weight: the most concrete explanatory chain in the corpus
passages.text: 10.5 KD: weight as evidencing coexistence, and “gravitation” renamed. KD ch. 3.11 gives the JV/MVD doctrine of §10.1–10.2 its most explicit form, including the one place in the corpus where the word gurutvākarṣaṇ (gravitation) is named and re-defined (our translations).

passages.heading: 10-mass-and-weight-the-most-concrete-explanatory-chain-in-the-corpus
passages.section: 10. Mass and weight: the most concrete explanatory chain in the corpus
passages.text: What MD says:

passages.heading: 10-mass-and-weight-the-most-concrete-explanatory-chain-in-the-corpus
passages.section: 10. Mass and weight: the most concrete explanatory chain in the corpus
passages.text: The whole of weight is the arrangement (vinyās) occurring in the course of evidencing coexistence with the Earth — weight is found to be animated by coexistence (KD, p. 103).

passages.heading: 10-mass-and-weight-the-most-concrete-explanatory-chain-in-the-corpus
passages.section: 10. Mass and weight: the most concrete explanatory chain in the corpus
passages.text: A solid object falling from above is the arrangement occurring with the Earth, in the effect of that object’s evidencing its coexistence with the Earth; this arrangement is what has been given the name “gravitation” — in reality it is only the arrangement of a solid evidencing coexistence with a solid. From “gravitation” runs the conception of small and big, but seen as coexistence, each thing is complete together with its own environment, and there simply is no small or big (KD, p. 104).

passages.heading: 10-mass-and-weight-the-most-concrete-explanatory-chain-in-the-corpus
passages.section: 10. Mass and weight: the most concrete explanatory chain in the corpus
passages.text: This tendency is found to remain bounded (maryādit) up to this Earth’s own environment; the Earth too is complete together with its own environment (KD, p. 104).

passages.heading: 10-mass-and-weight-the-most-concrete-explanatory-chain-in-the-corpus
passages.section: 10. Mass and weight: the most concrete explanatory chain in the corpus
passages.text: Molecules form when atoms join on the basis of the mid-particles’ mutual attraction-force, operating through magnetic-force-endowment; molecules are thereby naturally weight-endowed, and because of this weight, one molecule tends to join another while staying at the definite good distance (KD, p. 103).

passages.heading: 10-mass-and-weight-the-most-concrete-explanatory-chain-in-the-corpus
passages.section: 10. Mass and weight: the most concrete explanatory chain in the corpus
passages.text: Our reading, pulled together (§10.1–10.5): weight/gravitation is, by explicit textual statement, not a property of matter in isolation and not something satta imparts. It is a name for a tendency units display toward each other — specifically, a tendency to combine into larger compositions (atoms→molecules→bodies) — that only becomes “evident” once more than one unit is in mutual relation. KD’s contribution (claims 2–3) is to make the reversal of standard gravitation fully explicit: falling is not attraction by a larger mass but a body’s evidencing of coexistence with the Earth; the small/big asymmetry that makes Newtonian gravitation asymmetric is dismissed as an artifact of the “relative method”; and — most testably — the tendency is bounded to the Earth’s own environment rather than universal. That last clause puts KD in direct, statable conflict with universal gravitation (flagged in §15).

passages.heading: 11-indestructibility-nothing-is-created-nothing-is-annihilated
passages.section: 11. Indestructibility: nothing is created, nothing is annihilated
passages.text: 11. Indestructibility: nothing is created, nothing is annihilated

passages.heading: 11-indestructibility-nothing-is-created-nothing-is-annihilated
passages.section: 11. Indestructibility: nothing is created, nothing is annihilated
passages.text: This theme is stated independently in all five texts and functions as the darshan’s analogue of a conservation law — though what is conserved is units, not mass or energy as quantities.

passages.heading: 11-indestructibility-nothing-is-created-nothing-is-annihilated
passages.section: 11. Indestructibility: nothing is created, nothing is annihilated
passages.text: What MD says:

passages.heading: 11-indestructibility-nothing-is-created-nothing-is-annihilated
passages.section: 11. Indestructibility: nothing is created, nothing is annihilated
passages.text: Existence implies beingness and indestructibility (SB, p. 49).

passages.heading: 11-indestructibility-nothing-is-created-nothing-is-annihilated
passages.section: 11. Indestructibility: nothing is created, nothing is annihilated
passages.text: Every unit is endowed with the dharma of existence, evidenced by the indestructibility of units — all that occurs is merely change and development; dharma means that from which one cannot be separated, and since existence is coexistence, this indestructibility is itself the ultimate dharma (SB, p. 50).

passages.heading: 11-indestructibility-nothing-is-created-nothing-is-annihilated
passages.section: 11. Indestructibility: nothing is created, nothing is annihilated
passages.text: Even after fragmenting an atomic particle into countless parts, every fragment is still called “one” — demonstrating that annihilation or obliteration of anything is impossible; in existence there is no entity that “comes into being,” nor anything that “ceases to be” (SB, p. 103).

passages.heading: 11-indestructibility-nothing-is-created-nothing-is-annihilated
passages.section: 11. Indestructibility: nothing is created, nothing is annihilated
passages.text: From ancient times till now, all research, experiment, and conjecture on partitioning and division can be summarised as: nothing can be annihilated by progressive fragmentation (AVD, pp. 69–70).

passages.heading: 11-indestructibility-nothing-is-created-nothing-is-annihilated
passages.section: 11. Indestructibility: nothing is created, nothing is annihilated
passages.text: An entity’s decomposition does not mean annihilation of its respective constituents — existence neither decreases nor increases (AVD, p. 245; restated at p. 275: existence is therefore free from profit and loss, and thus indestructible).

passages.heading: 11-indestructibility-nothing-is-created-nothing-is-annihilated
passages.section: 11. Indestructibility: nothing is created, nothing is annihilated
passages.text: However far we subdivide units (particles), it will only increase their number, without anything getting annihilated (AVD, pp. 247–248).

passages.heading: 11-indestructibility-nothing-is-created-nothing-is-annihilated
passages.section: 11. Indestructibility: nothing is created, nothing is annihilated
passages.text: Every entity in its fundamental form is indestructible, no matter how many changes or results occur — this is the basis of the stability of the whole of existence (JVD, p. 82).

passages.heading: 11-indestructibility-nothing-is-created-nothing-is-annihilated
passages.section: 11. Indestructibility: nothing is created, nothing is annihilated
passages.text: Physical entities continue to exist and are never annihilated; they only manifest as chemical entities, a process called chemical resonance (rasaynik urmi) (JV, p. 125).

passages.heading: 11-indestructibility-nothing-is-created-nothing-is-annihilated
passages.section: 11. Indestructibility: nothing is created, nothing is annihilated
passages.text: There is no annihilation or absence of matter, mun, vritti, chitta, buddhi, or atma — they exist only in varying degrees of development and awakening (MVD, p. 299).

passages.heading: 11-indestructibility-nothing-is-created-nothing-is-annihilated
passages.section: 11. Indestructibility: nothing is created, nothing is annihilated
passages.text: Our reading: the corpus’s conservation principle is countability, not quantity: divide a unit as many times as you like and each fragment is still “one” — still bounded, still soaked in satta (cross-reference §4, claim 1: a unit cannot be annihilated because it cannot stop being soaked). What physics tracks as conservation of mass-energy the darshan replaces with a stronger, more ontological claim: composition and decomposition are the only real processes; creation ex nihilo and annihilation are not rare or difficult but strictly meaningless. This is the positive counterpart of §2.1’s Big Bang rejection — no origin event is needed because “coming into being” is not something that happens. Note the asymmetry with physics: pair annihilation (particle + antiparticle → photons) would presumably count for the darshan as transformation of units, not annihilation, but no text addresses anything like antimatter, so the reconciliation is untested. Claim 9 extends the same principle across the sentient side — jeevan’s faculties are as indestructible as particles, differing “only in degrees of development and awakening.”

passages.heading: 12-form-shape-volume-density-and-the-limits-of-measurement
passages.section: 12. Form — shape, volume, density — and the limits of measurement
passages.text: 12. Form — shape, volume, density — and the limits of measurement

passages.heading: 12-form-shape-volume-density-and-the-limits-of-measurement
passages.section: 12. Form — shape, volume, density — and the limits of measurement
passages.text: The texts define every unit’s form (roop) by a fixed three-dimensional triple, and then make an explicit claim about which of the darshan’s quantities are measurable at all.

passages.heading: 12-form-shape-volume-density-and-the-limits-of-measurement
passages.section: 12. Form — shape, volume, density — and the limits of measurement
passages.text: What MD says:

passages.heading: 12-form-shape-volume-density-and-the-limits-of-measurement
passages.section: 12. Form — shape, volume, density — and the limits of measurement
passages.text: Form is understood in terms of shape, volume, and density (SB, p. 65; repeated as the first of the four dimensions of atomic bodies at SB p. 86, and as a definition at MVD, p. 50: form in all four orders is determined by differentiation of shape, volume, and density).

passages.heading: 12-form-shape-volume-density-and-the-limits-of-measurement
passages.section: 12. Form — shape, volume, density — and the limits of measurement
passages.text: An object, in itself, is its shape, volume, and density — this is the very framework of a unit, defining its boundary; every unit is bounded on all sides, with Omnipotence seen on all sides of it (SB, p. 249).

passages.heading: 12-form-shape-volume-density-and-the-limits-of-measurement
passages.section: 12. Form — shape, volume, density — and the limits of measurement
passages.text: Compositions made of atoms of a particular kind may vary in size, shape, volume, or density, but their essence remains constant — the intrinsic properties and nature of objects, expressed as their “essence,” do not increase or decrease despite variation in measurement, weight, or volume (SB, p. 119).

passages.heading: 12-form-shape-volume-density-and-the-limits-of-measurement
passages.section: 12. Form — shape, volume, density — and the limits of measurement
passages.text: Shape, volume, and density can be measured, and it has become possible to measure positive and negative charges — but not all properties can be measured: mediative power, which underlies the natural state and mediativeness, has not been measurable (SB, p. 250).

passages.heading: 12-form-shape-volume-density-and-the-limits-of-measurement
passages.section: 12. Form — shape, volume, density — and the limits of measurement
passages.text: An object’s volume is always more than what its shape projects to the eye, and its density even more than shape and volume — so whatever we see with our eyes, its entirety is not captured by the eyes (AVD, p. 199).

passages.heading: 12-form-shape-volume-density-and-the-limits-of-measurement
passages.section: 12. Form — shape, volume, density — and the limits of measurement
passages.text: The shape, volume, and density of jeevan, a sentient unit, can be understood in the same context, since jeevan too is only an atom (AVD, p. 185).

passages.heading: 12-form-shape-volume-density-and-the-limits-of-measurement
passages.section: 12. Form — shape, volume, density — and the limits of measurement
passages.text: However powerful the lens — showing something a billion or trillion times larger — instrument-evidence (yantra pramāṇ) cannot exceed the eyes: make the eye a billion times more effective, and only that much more meaning comes out (KD, p. 133).

passages.heading: 12-form-shape-volume-density-and-the-limits-of-measurement
passages.section: 12. Form — shape, volume, density — and the limits of measurement
passages.text: Even mechanically-derived direction- and time-related activity remains related to the human at root; hence at the root of instrument-evidence, the human alone is the evidence (KD, p. 130); elsewhere KD presses the same point against science’s self-description — the instrument became treated as the principal evidence, with responsibility shifted from the human onto instruments, though with instruments no reasoning is possible at all, because what an instrument does, it keeps doing again and again (KD, p. 86).

passages.heading: 12-form-shape-volume-density-and-the-limits-of-measurement
passages.section: 12. Form — shape, volume, density — and the limits of measurement
passages.text: Our reading: density is the third coordinate of unit-hood itself — form is shape-volume-density, and that triple is what bounds a unit off from the satta surrounding it (tying directly to §4’s “distance is satta”). Claim 4 then draws the corpus’s clearest line between what measurement can and cannot reach, and it maps exactly onto the §5/§8 force inventory: form dimensions — measurable; positive/negative (generative/degenerative) charges — measurable, and the texts credit physics with having measured them; mediative power — not measurable. This is the darshan’s own explanation of why the fifth force of §5’s table is absent from physics’ inventory: instrument-based method can only register what varies (charges, “more and less,” §8), and the mediative is definitionally the non-varying reference point of the variation. Claim 3’s essence-invariance (“ironness” constant under any change of size, weight, or volume) plays the role that intensive properties play in physics, but is extended into a metaphysical claim. Claim 5 adds an epistemic ordering — eyes capture part of shape, less of volume, less again of density — grounding the recurring argument that perception, and by extension instrumentation, systematically under-samples even measurable form. Claim 7 supplies the missing premise connecting the two: instruments are amplified eyes and nothing more, so AVD’s limits on the eye transfer to every microscope and detector — which is why, for the darshan, no instrument could ever register the mediative (claim 4) and understanding (samajh) rather than magnification is the required instrument.

passages.heading: 13-time-kaal-brief-cross-reference
passages.section: 13. Time (kaal) — brief cross-reference
passages.text: 13. Time (kaal) — brief cross-reference

passages.heading: 13-time-kaal-brief-cross-reference
passages.section: 13. Time (kaal) — brief cross-reference
passages.text: Time is treated at length in the existing Nature of Time study; this note only pulls the handful of claims most relevant to the satta–unit physical-interaction question, for completeness.

passages.heading: 13-time-kaal-brief-cross-reference
passages.section: 13. Time (kaal) — brief cross-reference
passages.text: What MD says:

passages.heading: 13-time-kaal-brief-cross-reference
passages.section: 13. Time (kaal) — brief cross-reference
passages.text: Time (kaal) is the duration of an activity (MVD, p. 34).

passages.heading: 13-time-kaal-brief-cross-reference
passages.section: 13. Time (kaal) — brief cross-reference
passages.text: KD opens with the identical definition, then critiques clock-time: time was originally recognised on the basis of one continuously recurring activity-cycle — the Earth’s one rotational motion completing day-and-night, named “the day,” then divided into 24 parts, then 60, and so on. In this dividing, the activity itself was forgotten and time became treated as primary, an error from which further problems were born. Time is ever-present (nitya vartmān); the present, as reality, is coexistence itself, and it is to the present that the name kaal has been given (KD, p. 134).

passages.heading: 13-time-kaal-brief-cross-reference
passages.section: 13. Time (kaal) — brief cross-reference
passages.text: Coexistence is trikaalabadh — a timeless truth valid across all three times (SB, p. 48).

passages.heading: 13-time-kaal-brief-cross-reference
passages.section: 13. Time (kaal) — brief cross-reference
passages.text: Absolute energy differs from matter in that absolute energy is present in every time, place, and object, with no place or object ever found or proven devoid of it — whereas places devoid of matter do exist, though no time devoid of matter has been proven (MVD, p. 41).

passages.heading: 13-time-kaal-brief-cross-reference
passages.section: 13. Time (kaal) — brief cross-reference
passages.text: Our reading: time is defined strictly as a property of unit-activity (kriya), exactly parallel to how §2–§3 above define pressure, force, and weight as unit-mutuality phenomena. Satta is kriya-shunya (actionless) and therefore, by the same logic, timeless — not because it exists “before” or “outside” time in a cosmological sense, but because time is definitionally absent wherever activity is absent. This is structurally the same move the texts make for force and weight: locate the physical-sounding predicate at the unit level, deny it of the ground, by definition rather than by discovery.

passages.heading: 14-synthesis-the-structure-of-the-darshans-physics
passages.section: 14. Synthesis: the structure of the darshan’s physics
passages.text: 14. Synthesis: the structure of the darshan’s physics

passages.heading: 14-synthesis-the-structure-of-the-darshans-physics
passages.section: 14. Synthesis: the structure of the darshan’s physics
passages.text: Read section by section, the corpus can look like a list of unconnected physics opinions. Read together, §2–§13 are one construction applied uniformly. This entire section is our reading — a synthesis built on the claims listed above, not a set of textual claims in its own right. It states the construction once (14.1), gives it a formal reading that organises it more tightly than paraphrase can (14.2), isolates the single claim in it that ordinary physics does not already hold in some form (14.3), and closes with the reference map (14.4).

passages.heading: 14-synthesis-the-structure-of-the-darshans-physics
passages.section: 14. Synthesis: the structure of the darshan’s physics
passages.text: 14.1 The repeated move. Across pressure and cosmogony (§2), force (§3–4), atomic structure and states of matter (§6), charge/excitation (§8), heat/magnetism/electricity/radioactivity (§9), weight (§10), indestructibility (§11), form/density (§12), and time (§13), the texts do the same three things every time:

passages.heading: 14-synthesis-the-structure-of-the-darshans-physics
passages.section: 14. Synthesis: the structure of the darshan’s physics
passages.text: Deny the predicate of satta directly and explicitly — actionless, pressureless, wave-free, weightless (zero-attraction), timeless, non-transforming.

passages.heading: 14-synthesis-the-structure-of-the-darshans-physics
passages.section: 14. Synthesis: the structure of the darshan’s physics
passages.text: Locate the predicate in unit-to-unit mutuality instead — pressure from environmental influence; charge from generative/degenerative imbalance around a mediating centre; weight from units’ tendency to combine; time from activity’s duration.

passages.heading: 14-synthesis-the-structure-of-the-darshans-physics
passages.section: 14. Synthesis: the structure of the darshan’s physics
passages.text: Name the bond between satta and units with force-like vocabulary anyway — “forcefulness,” “magnetic forcefulness,” “energisation” — but frame it as an eternal endowment/unfolding, not an event, force-transmission, or efficient cause.

passages.heading: 14-synthesis-the-structure-of-the-darshans-physics
passages.section: 14. Synthesis: the structure of the darshan’s physics
passages.text: Steps 1 and 2 are repeated independently across SB, MVD, JV, and KD, and support a relational-dispositional axiom: physical effects become manifest in mutuality between definite units; no such predicate belongs to the actionless ground. This does not leave the units as predicate-free nodes. The texts attribute boundary, constitution, state, force-capacity, order, and dharma to the bearer, while MVD p. 40 defines heat, sound, electricity, pressure, waves, and fields as relative power that does not become apparent without unit mutuality. KD p. 102’s bal/shakti pair (§7.1) gives the same distinction dynamically: force is the property-endowed unit in state, power is the inseparable property evident in motion. Step 3 is the one place the system’s vocabulary pulls against itself (§15, first bullet) — though 14.2 suggests the tension is terminological rather than structural.

passages.heading: 14-synthesis-the-structure-of-the-darshans-physics
passages.section: 14. Synthesis: the structure of the darshan’s physics
passages.text: 14.2 A formal reading: units as objects, mutuality as morphisms, satta as the unit object. This subsection is our interpretive frame, not the texts’. It is included because it resolves two of §15’s open tensions and states the darshan’s position in vocabulary a physics-literate reader already has.

passages.heading: 14-synthesis-the-structure-of-the-darshans-physics
passages.section: 14. Synthesis: the structure of the darshan’s physics
passages.text: Take units (ikai) as the objects of a category and mutualities as its morphisms. Objects retain typed structure — boundary, constitution, order, state, and capacities — while morphisms carry the actual reflection, relative influence, exchange, or composition through which those capacities become evident. A unit’s relational profile can therefore identify and test its kind (jaati, §6) without exhausting what the texts say the unit is. This is a narrower affinity with Machian, gauge-relational, and relational-quantum approaches than the claim that only relations exist: the comparison concerns interaction-indexed observables, not svabhav, dharma, development, or value.

passages.heading: 14-synthesis-the-structure-of-the-darshans-physics
passages.section: 14. Synthesis: the structure of the darshan’s physics
passages.text: Satta then maps not to any object in the category but to the monoidal unit — the “empty context” I with which every object composes without change (A ≅ I⊗A ≅ A⊗I). Every one of the texts’ descriptions checks against this role, clause by clause: satta “doesn’t prove to be a unit” (§2, claim 2 — precisely: I is not a system); it is formless (no internal structure); it is omnipresent and in-between (every composition of units factors through it — §4, claim 5’s “the definite distance between particles is formless existence”); and “saturation” is the unitor — an isomorphism that is always already in place, structural rather than dynamical. On this reading the magnetic-force knot dissolves: the texts reach for force vocabulary because ordinary language has no word for a structural enabling condition, but the bond’s logical role is a unit law, not a dynamical arrow. “Being soaked itself is forcefulness” (§4, claim 1) becomes exactly right — the bond does nothing over and above being the condition of composition.

passages.heading: 14-synthesis-the-structure-of-the-darshans-physics
passages.section: 14. Synthesis: the structure of the darshan’s physics
passages.text: Three further pieces fall into place under the same reading:

passages.heading: 14-synthesis-the-structure-of-the-darshans-physics
passages.section: 14. Synthesis: the structure of the darshan’s physics
passages.text: Indestructibility (§11) is the absence of a zero object: there are no morphisms from or to nothing. Composition and decomposition are rearrangements within the tensor structure; creation ex nihilo and annihilation are not rare or difficult — they are ungrammatical. This is why the texts treat “nothing can be annihilated” as a logical point about counting (“every fragment is still called ‘one’,” §11 claim 3), not an empirical discovery.

passages.heading: 14-synthesis-the-structure-of-the-darshans-physics
passages.section: 14. Synthesis: the structure of the darshan’s physics
passages.text: Time (§13) is defined on morphisms — durations of activity — not as a background parameter. This is the process-first ordering that categorical approaches to physics also adopt: processes are primary, states derivative.

passages.heading: 14-synthesis-the-structure-of-the-darshans-physics
passages.section: 14. Synthesis: the structure of the darshan’s physics
passages.text: The Five Forces table (§5) and the universal constitution principle (§6, claim 3) are claims that a structure-preserving map — a functor — exists between the insentient domain and the sentient one: same nucleus-and-orbits architecture, mapped across orders, not shared substance. This settles §15’s second bullet toward “analogical,” but with a precise sense of analogy that is stronger than loose metaphor: the claim is that the structure transfers exactly, whatever the entities are.

passages.heading: 14-synthesis-the-structure-of-the-darshans-physics
passages.section: 14. Synthesis: the structure of the darshan’s physics
passages.text: 14.3 What the darshan asserts that physics does not: the mediative as primitive, and the development arrow. The relational axiom of 14.1–14.2 is congruent with live physics programs; it contributes an ontology, not new machinery. The mediative doctrine (§5, §8, §12) is different in kind, and it is the corpus’s one structural claim that ordinary physics denies rather than already believes. Physics treats equilibrium as emergent (a statistical fact about many interactions) and treats the reference point of any ± opposition as conventional (a choice of zero, a gauge choice). The darshan asserts the reference is ontologically primitive: a real third alongside every generative/degenerative pair, doing continuous regulatory work (§8, claim 2), and unmeasurable by definition, because measurement only registers variation and the mediative is the invariant of the variation (§12, claim 4). Stated physics-side, the general principle on offer is: every observable two-valued variation presupposes a non-observable invariant that actively parameterises it. The nearest analogues in physics are the connection/curvature distinction (curvature is measured; the connection itself is not) and renormalisation-group fixed points — but in both cases physics derives the invariant from the dynamics, whereas the darshan posits it as the more fundamental term and derives the dynamics (charge, excitation, decline, resolution) from distance to it.

passages.heading: 14-synthesis-the-structure-of-the-darshans-physics
passages.section: 14. Synthesis: the structure of the darshan’s physics
passages.text: KD both sharpens and strains this claim. It sharpens the diagnosis: physics misses the mediative because “all these studies are based on excited motion alone” (§7.1, claim 2) — measurement registers variation, the mediative is what holds in the unvaried state. But §8’s claim 9 also gives the mediative an explicitly dynamical job description: a two-way restoring influence that pulls orbital particles back to a set-point “good distance” against displacement in either direction. That is, formally, a restoring force about an equilibrium separation — the kind of statement physics can model (a potential well) and does measure the consequences of (bound states, vibrational spectra). So KD makes the mediative doctrine less insulated than SB leaves it: a regulator that fixes an equilibrium distance has observable signatures even if the regulator itself is “not measurable.” The paper should note this as the corpus’s nearest approach to a falsifiable clause — and that physics would answer: the restoring behaviour around equilibrium separations is real and well-measured, and derives from the ± interactions themselves, needing no third primitive.

passages.heading: 14-synthesis-the-structure-of-the-darshans-physics
passages.section: 14. Synthesis: the structure of the darshan’s physics
passages.text: The full KD translation surfaces a second physics-denying claim, distinct from the mediative: the direction of spontaneous change. Physics’ second law says isolated systems drift toward equilibrium in the sense of disorder; the darshan asserts a universal drift with the opposite sign (§8, claim 10). The same monotone appears as §7’s rising vibrational motion with rising stability, §6’s development progression through species toward constitutional completeness, and §9.2’s Sun cooling toward its natural state — that last being simply this arrow applied to a star. So the corpus has two teleological primitives, and they compose: the mediative supplies the local restoring tendency (equilibration about set-points), and the development arrow supplies the global drift (successive set-points ascending toward completeness). A physics reader should be told plainly that this arrow runs against the entropic one, and that the darshan would answer the obvious objection (order increases locally only by exporting disorder) by denying the bookkeeping premise — for it, de-excitation is not export of disorder but approach to the natural state, which costs nothing.

passages.heading: 14-synthesis-the-structure-of-the-darshans-physics
passages.section: 14. Synthesis: the structure of the darshan’s physics
passages.text: Two liabilities, flagged for the paper: (i) the unmeasurability doctrine insulates the mediative claim from every empirical test — a physics reader will identify this immediately, and the paper should concede it rather than soften it (with the KD qualification above); (ii) §11’s conservation of units (countability) conflicts with particle creation and annihilation in quantum field theory unless the darshan’s “particles” sit below field quanta — a question the texts never face (no antimatter, no field-quantum vocabulary anywhere in the corpus).

passages.section: 15. Open interpretive tensions (flag for the paper, not yet resolved)
passages.text: This section, like §14, is entirely our reading — flagged tensions and open questions, not textual claims.

passages.heading: 15-open-interpretive-tensions-flag-for-the-paper-not-yet-resolved
passages.section: 15. Open interpretive tensions (flag for the paper, not yet resolved)
passages.text: “Magnetic force” vs. actionless doctrine. SB literally calls the saturation bond’s forcefulness “magnetic force” (चुम्बकीय बल, p. 61) while also insisting satta is actionless and non-transforming. The texts do not reconcile these in the same passage. The most charitable reading (used in The Ontology of Coexistence §1.2) is that “magnetic force” names a standing, eternal endowment rather than a transmitted quantity — but this is an interpretive choice, not something the text states outright. §14.2’s formal reading (saturation as unit law, not dynamical arrow) makes the choice principled rather than merely charitable. Worth a dedicated footnote or subsection wherever this note’s material gets folded into a published study.

passages.heading: 15-open-interpretive-tensions-flag-for-the-paper-not-yet-resolved
passages.section: 15. Open interpretive tensions (flag for the paper, not yet resolved)
passages.text: Five Forces table — descriptive or analogical? SB p. 85 does not say whether it is claiming physics is incomplete without a fifth (“mediative”) force, or simply using the four-force inventory as a structural analogy for jeevan’s five faculties. The strong/weak interaction rows get no independent gloss anywhere else in the corpus (only the table itself) — thin evidentiary support compared to electromagnetic/gravitational, which are discussed extensively elsewhere. §14.2’s functor reading favours the analogical horn, with a precise sense of “analogy” (structure transfers exactly; substance does not).

passages.heading: 15-open-interpretive-tensions-flag-for-the-paper-not-yet-resolved
passages.section: 15. Open interpretive tensions (flag for the paper, not yet resolved)
passages.text: Āvesh as evaluative vocabulary. SB ties charge/excitation definitionally close to “problem” and its absence to “resolution” — useful for the book’s thesis (Resolution-Centred Materialism) but worth flagging as a place where physics vocabulary is doing double duty as ethical/soteriological vocabulary; MD-Mapping’s own definition of āvesh (“deluded conduct-tendency; motion toward decline”) builds the evaluation into the word. The contextual rule (§8: ± imbalance = charge; disturbed condition = excited state) resolves most instances, but a reader could still ask whether āvesh is one concept with two faces or two concepts sharing one word — the texts treat the ± imbalance and the disturbed state as one phenomenon, which is itself a substantive claim.

passages.heading: 15-open-interpretive-tensions-flag-for-the-paper-not-yet-resolved
passages.section: 15. Open interpretive tensions (flag for the paper, not yet resolved)
passages.text: No subatomic-particle vocabulary, no periodic table, no atomic numbers. Electron, proton, neutron do not appear in SB, MVD, JV, AVD, JVD, or KD. “Particles” (ansh) are counted generically, and no named element (hydrogen, iron, gold, etc.) is ever given a specific particle count — only a growth rule (§6) now supplemented by KD’s structural constraints (§6.4a: minimum 1+1, nucleus ≥ orbits, four-orbit equilibrium) and KD p. 55’s acknowledgement of the “108 species” inventory as a human claim. Any comparison to modern atomic physics needs to keep the remaining gap explicit: the darshan has the shape of a shell model, and now some of its inequalities, but still no per-element numbers (no analogue of “carbon = 6”). The one place a specific, named, fixed structure does appear is jeevan itself — exactly four orbits plus nucleus, ten activities, psychologically named rather than numbered (§6.4) — which is a special case, not the general insentient-atom model. (Curiously, KD’s nucleus ≥ orbits inequality holds under the natural modern mapping: if orbital ansh = electrons and madhyansh = nucleons, then “at least as many in the middle as in the orbits, possibly more” is exactly A ≥ Z — true of every neutral atom, with equality only at hydrogen-1, which is also KD’s stated minimum atom (1+1). Whether this is insight or coincidence cannot be settled from the texts, since ansh is never identified with any named particle — but it is the corpus’s single most striking numerical agreement with standard atomic physics and deserves a paragraph in the paper.)

passages.heading: 15-open-interpretive-tensions-flag-for-the-paper-not-yet-resolved
passages.section: 15. Open interpretive tensions (flag for the paper, not yet resolved)
passages.text: Is particle-level restlessness (§6.8) universal, or specific to sub-threshold particles? KD’s “whirling in the void” passage (p. 56) is stated for atoms still under development; whether the same claim would apply to, say, a buddhi-particle hypothetically separated from an already-completed jeevan atom is not addressed anywhere in the corpus.

passages.heading: 15-open-interpretive-tensions-flag-for-the-paper-not-yet-resolved
passages.section: 15. Open interpretive tensions (flag for the paper, not yet resolved)
passages.text: Does the nucleus/orbit functional split plus subtlety gradient (§6.6) generalise beyond jeevan? MVD names the gradient (mun→atma) only for the sentient atom; whether an ordinary (insentient) atom’s nucleus particles are, in some lesser sense, also “more developed” than its orbital particles, or whether the gradient reading is jeevan-specific, is not settled by the texts consulted here.

passages.heading: 15-open-interpretive-tensions-flag-for-the-paper-not-yet-resolved
passages.section: 15. Open interpretive tensions (flag for the paper, not yet resolved)
passages.text: “Overfull” is undefined. SB p. 259 rests radioactivity (and the entire solar model of §9.2) on atoms being “overfull,” but no text says overfull relative to what — there is no stated maximum particle count per orbit or per nucleus (consistent with §6’s missing numbers, but here the gap is doing explanatory work). Also unreconciled: §9.2’s Sun-as-cooling-toward-natural-state reverses the direction of standard stellar physics, and the texts never engage fusion as an energy source at all.

passages.heading: 15-open-interpretive-tensions-flag-for-the-paper-not-yet-resolved
passages.section: 15. Open interpretive tensions (flag for the paper, not yet resolved)
passages.text: Jeevan’s four orbits vs. insentient atoms’ open-ended orbit count — now partially answered by KD. MVD p. 78 allows ordinary atoms “first, second, third, fourth, and so on” orbits (unspecified upper bound) but fixes jeevan at exactly four, without explanation. KD p. 56 (§6.4a) supplies what looks like the missing law: orbit counts above four tend to decrease and below four tend to increase — four is the equilibrium of the orbit-count dynamics. On that reading, constitutional completeness is the stable fixed point of atomic development, and jeevan’s four orbits are not an arbitrary cap but the attractor every developing atom moves toward — which meshes exactly with §6.4b’s prasthāpan–visthāpan (the particle-transfer process that moves atoms through species) and with MVD p. 78’s open-ended counts for atoms still en route. Still open: why four is the equilibrium (KD asserts the tendency, not its ground), and whether the §1.6.1 (gathanpurnata) material glosses completeness as specifically the four-orbit configuration.

passages.heading: 15-open-interpretive-tensions-flag-for-the-paper-not-yet-resolved
passages.section: 15. Open interpretive tensions (flag for the paper, not yet resolved)
passages.text: KD’s gravitation is local, not universal. KD p. 104 bounds the falling-tendency “up to this Earth’s environment,” with each body “complete with its own environment” (§10.5). Taken at face value this denies universal gravitation — yet §9.4 (KD p. 76) has the planets maintaining “good distance” around the Sun, which universal gravitation explains and a strictly Earth-bounded tendency does not. The texts do not connect the two passages. Options for the paper: (a) “good distance” order among planets is a separate, non-gravitational principle for KD (consistent with JV’s zero-attraction doctrine, §10.1); (b) the boundedness claim concerns only the falling arrangement, not inter-body order. The corpus underdetermines the choice.

passages.section: Method note (for reproducibility)
passages.text: Primary texts were converted to plain text with pdftotext -layout, and page numbers were cross-checked two ways: (1) internal footer markers (“page-NN”) embedded in the MVD and JVD PDFs, present roughly every page; (2) for SB and JV, where footers were not machine-readable, page indices were calibrated against page citations already established and used consistently in The Ontology of Coexistence (e.g. “SB, p. 48,” “SB, p. 62,” “MVD, p. 40”) by locating the matching English sentence and checking the offset was constant (confirmed: PDF page-splitting index + 1 = printed page number, holding across more than five independent check-points in SB). The claims above are paraphrased from the English portion of the bilingual PDFs; Hindi originals were consulted for the technical terms glossed in brackets. Before quoting any claim verbatim in a catalog Study, re-verify the exact wording against the source PDF via Scripts/_quote_tool.py verify --study <Slug> — the paraphrase here is for readability and is not itself citable wording.

passages.heading: method-note-for-reproducibility
passages.section: Method note (for reproducibility)
passages.text: KD (Manav Karm Darshan, v5) requires a separate protocol. The PDF is Hindi-only (no English translation exists in the References), and its embedded font’s character map is corrupted, so machine-extracted text is systematically garbled (e.g. त/स्/ि cycle, श↔र्) — the text layer was used only to locate candidate pages by cipher-adjusted term search, never to transcribe. All KD passages cited here were read visually from rendered page images and translated by us. The full working English translation (front matter + chapters 1–3) is in References/Madhyasth-Darshan/KD-Karm-Darshan-English/KD-Karm-Darshan-English.md, with [p. NN] printed-page markers, _page-images/ Hindi page renders, and term decisions in KD-Glossary-Additions.md + KD-Translation-Glossary.xlsx; inline KD claims in this note should be read against that file, which supersedes them where wording differs, and all remain working translations pending a published English edition. Page numbers cited are the printed page numbers in the running headers (calibration: printed page = PDF page − 25, constant across all pages checked). Two fixed terminology conventions: āvesh/āveshit is translated contextually — “charge” where the text concerns the positive/negative (generative/degenerative) imbalance of atoms, “excited/excitation” where it concerns a unit’s disturbed state as against its neutral/natural state (rule stated in full in §8’s terminology note; SB’s published English uses “charge” for both and glosses the state sense “excited (charged)” at p. 257; MD-Mapping carries both readings); and śram = effort (MD-Mapping’s notes: “We are using ‘effort’ for shram in the sense of shram-gati-parinam”), with “labour” reserved for economic compounds (श्रम मूल्य = labour value). Chapter 3 (printed pp. 53–153) is fully translated in the combined file; ch. 3.12 (reflection–projection) proved on full translation to be chiefly epistemological — teaching/study as reflection–projection — with heat transfer as one species of the general category (noted in §9.4).
